title: My Dad's Emotional Reaction to My Art
summary: A roughly 3:14 first-person account of shame, anger and reconciliation around the narrator’s father visiting an art show. He imagines the father embarrassed by his crude Korean stage performance, reports the father questioning why anyone buys the paintings, becomes 16 again emotionally at age 41, rejects him, then resents that other relatives persuade him to attend. In a green/confessional room the expected criticism gives way to softness, English praise and an aging close-up that lets the narrator feel seen beneath facade and showboating. Every crude, angry, family, language, aging and praise detail remains; Korean/profanity masks, private identities, objective rankings, medical inference, the damaged final quote and the line-level voice remain unresolved.
